identification.summary: Pakistan-linked cyber espionage cluster that Microsoft names Viridian Vortex and maps to Transparent Tribe, APT36, SideCopy, MYTHIC LEOPARD and Storm-0156 [S1]. Open reporting describes it as a suspected Pakistan-based group operating since at least 2013 that focuses on Indian government, defense and related targets [S5][S6]. Security press describes SideCopy, active since at least 2019, as assessed to be a subdivision of Transparent Tribe [S7].
identification.firstObserved: Since at least 2013 per Security Affairs/Hacker News coverage of 2025 reporting [S5][S6]. SideCopy sub-cluster: since at least 2019 [S7].
identification.notes: Microsoft's mapping lumps Transparent Tribe, APT36 and SideCopy under one name [S1]; other vendors treat SideCopy as a related sub-cluster, so facts attributed to SideCopy should not be silently merged with Transparent Tribe-only reporting [S7]. Press coverage also lists the name Earth Karkaddan for the group [S5][S6]. I could not open Microsoft's own Viridian Vortex analysis; the mapping is taken from Microsoft's naming file [S1].

attribution.confidence: Vendors describe the group only as suspected Pakistan-based or of Pakistani origin [S5][S6]. Talos assessed with high confidence that a Pakistani web hosting provider (Zain Hosting) was used to deploy and operate components of Transparent Tribe infrastructure [S2]. No government attribution to a named Pakistani agency was found in sources reviewed.
attribution.basis: Pakistani-hosted infrastructure [S2]; consistent targeting of Indian government, military and education [S2][S5]; Microsoft country designation of Pakistan in its naming file [S1].

objectives: Espionage against Indian government, defense and related organizations [S5][S7]. Talos noted a 2021-2022 deviation toward students at Indian educational institutions [S2]. ESET reported Android spyware aimed at users in India and Pakistan, likely with military or political ties [S4].

sectors: Policy, research and critical infrastructure (per Aryaka via press)
targeting.notes: Indian government entities using BOSS Linux were targeted in 2025 [S5][S6]. Indian defense and government-aligned organizations were targeted with Windows and Linux RATs reported in February 2026 [S7]. ESET geolocated over 150 victims in its CapraRAT campaign [S4].

capabilities.summary: Spear-phishing with malicious documents or links [S2]; CrimsonRAT for long-term access [S2]; trojanized Android messaging apps (MeetsApp, MeetUp) delivering CapraRAT, with a suspected honeytrap lure [S4]; malicious Linux .desktop files that open a decoy PDF while dropping a Go-based ELF backdoor with cron persistence and hard-coded C2 [S5][S6]; Geta RAT on Windows (LNK to HTA, mshta, in-memory execution), Python-based Ares RAT on Linux, and Go-based DeskRAT via a PowerPoint add-in with WebSocket C2 [S7]. Use of compromised legitimate domains to host HTA files was reported [S7].

campaigns.name: CrimsonRAT campaign against Indian students
campaigns.summary: Talos reported a campaign beginning around December 2021 against students at Indian educational institutions, a deviation from the usual government focus, delivering CrimsonRAT via spear-phishing documents; Talos assessed with high confidence that Zain Hosting was used for infrastructure [S2]. K7 Labs first observed the education targeting in May 2022 [S3].

campaigns.name: CapraRAT via trojanized messaging apps
campaigns.summary: ESET attributed to Transparent Tribe a campaign active since July 2022 distributing CapraRAT through trojanized MeetsApp and MeetUp apps from fake sites, with over 150 victims geolocated by ESET; a honeytrap lure is suspected [S4].

campaigns.name: BOSS Linux .desktop file campaign
campaigns.summary: Reporting described malicious .desktop shortcut files targeting Windows and BOSS Linux systems of Indian government entities; a sample shell script dropped a Go ELF backdoor, opened a decoy PDF, set cron persistence and contacted a hard-coded C2 [S5][S6].

campaigns.name: APT36 and SideCopy cross-platform RAT campaigns
campaigns.summary: Reporting described campaigns against Indian defense and government-aligned organizations using Geta RAT, Ares RAT and DeskRAT on Windows and Linux; DeskRAT use by APT36 was first documented by Sekoia and QiAnXin XLab in October 2025 per The Hacker News [S7].

diamond.adversary: Suspected Pakistan-based espionage group with a SideCopy sub-cluster; no named sponsor in sources reviewed [S5][S7].
diamond.capability: Spear-phishing, CrimsonRAT, CapraRAT, Geta/Ares/DeskRAT, Linux .desktop droppers [S2][S4][S5][S7].
diamond.infrastructure: Pakistani hosting provider Zain Hosting [S2]; hard-coded C2 domain in 2025 BOSS campaign [S5]; compromised legitimate domains hosting HTA files [S7]; fake distribution sites for Android apps [S4].
diamond.victim: Indian government, defense, education and students; Android users in India and Pakistan [S2][S4][S5][S7].
diamond.socioPolitical: Targeting pattern aligns with India-Pakistan strategic rivalry, but sources reviewed do not state the tasking explicitly; this is analyst inference from [S2][S5].
diamond.technology: Windows (LNK, HTA, mshta, Office add-ins), Linux (BOSS, .desktop files, Go and Python implants), and Android [S4][S5][S7].

gaps: Microsoft's own Viridian Vortex analysis was not opened; only the naming mapping was used [S1].
No government or vendor attribution to a specific Pakistani organization found.
Boundaries between Transparent Tribe, APT36 and SideCopy differ by vendor; Microsoft merges them [S1][S7].

MITRE ATT&CK page, Seqrite, Cyble, SentinelLabs, Nextron and Aryaka primary reports could not be fetched (web fetch failed); their content is known only through search summaries and is not cited as sources.
Exact publication dates of the Security Affairs and 2026 Hacker News articles were taken from URL and search context.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Step 1-2: relevant battlespace is Indian government/defense networks and personnel devices across Windows, BOSS/Linux and Android [S4][S5][S7]. Step 3: adversary uses phishing-led access with commodity-style RATs and cross-platform loaders, with Pakistani-hosted infrastructure [S2][S7]. MLCOA: continued spear-phishing of Indian government and defense with new lure formats and Linux payloads [S5][S7]. MDCOA: broader targeting of education, policy and critical-infrastructure organizations, or mobile-focused collection against military-linked users [S2][S4][S7]. Candidate indicators: .desktop files with double extensions, LNK/HTA chains using mshta, PPAM add-ins, cron persistence from unknown ELF binaries, WebSocket C2 [S5][S7].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: share indicators for Linux .desktop and HTA/LNK chains with partners operating Linux and mobile endpoints [S5][S7]. Authorities: any response beyond defensive hunting depends on legal authorities not addressed in the sources. Mission assurance: harden email gateways, restrict mshta and unsigned add-ins, monitor cron changes, and control sideloaded mobile apps [S4][S5][S7]. Coordination: align reporting with vendor naming differences (Microsoft vs. other vendors) to avoid duplicate tracking [S1][S7].
